correctness.rationale: Exact 2x2 expansion gives T_(lambda,u)(s,t,w)=(omega(u,w),0,lambda w+ut). Explicit composition gives F_(lambda mu,mu u,lambda v,omega(u,v)) and the triple-factor absorption law, so length at most two is proved without finite search. Nondegeneracy of the alternating form on K^2 proves every announced stratum is attainable. The strata are pairwise disjoint; counts and rank arguments have been reconstructed. Standalone finite-field enumeration of all pair products over F2, F4 and F8 and closure checks for F2,F4 agree with the formulas. Tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest recent full paper proves full semigroup generation only when the characteristic differs from two. It notes merely the characteristic-two scalar-kernel and traceless-image obstructions, not a finite or infinite characteristic-two classification, length bound, rank profile, or cardinality. The related published two-by-two prescribed-commutator graph result concerns counts of matrix pairs rather than compositions of inner-derivation operators. Searches for both alternate formulations and characteristic-two operator-composition semigroups did not locate a dominating or equivalent statement. The present conclusion therefore remains apparently original, with unindexed historical treatments as residual risk, not a priority certification.
residual_risks: An older equivalent result may be indexed under inner-derivation or Lie-adjoint operator-semigroup terminology not located by the search engines.

value.rationale: A 2026 paper demonstrates unexpectedly maximal Jordan multiplication semigroups but explicitly excludes characteristic two, where its short obstruction leaves a concrete natural classification gap. The exact classification, uniform word-length two bound and finite-field rank/cardinality spectrum answer what the degeneracy actually leaves, not just that full generation fails. The same structural law applies to all characteristic-two fields and the counting polynomial covers every finite field of that characteristic.
